harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the supplied handler on node1 via BusyBox inetd on TCP/9097. Sequential and concurrent clients from node2 return the correct responses, each connection receives a separate handler process, no handlers remain afterward, and the service persisted across one-at-a-time restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Installed the CentOS Stream 10-compatible EPEL BusyBox package providing inetd.
Configured inetd to run the supplied handler as nobody with nowait semantics.
Created and enabled legacy-inetd.service and permanently allowed TCP/9097 through firewalld.
Verified PING returns PONG, other input returns ERROR, and only one request is processed per connection.
Verified 16 simultaneous connections created 16 distinct handler processes, completed without failures, and left no processes behind.
Preserved the protocol note and existing OS release/kernel.
Safely restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Deploy the supplied stdio handler through inetd on node1 TCP/9097.
evidence.summary: BusyBox inetd is enabled and active, listens on 0.0.0.0:9097, and its nowait configuration invokes the supplied handler as nobody.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG; other lines return ERROR; one request is handled per connection.
evidence.summary: Remote tests from node2 returned PONG for PING and ERROR for other input; a two-line connection produced only one response.

evidence.requirement: Sequential and concurrent clients complete without leaving handler processes.
evidence.summary: Sixteen held connections produced 16 distinct handler PIDs; all clients passed and the final process check reported HANDLERS=none.

evidence.requirement: Preserve protocol notes and keep the installed OS release and kernel.
evidence.summary: The protocol-note checksum remained ec27c3ff8a76bef6fda09442e45105628cd20fbb0ad62c86528ba7443fdfd899. Both nodes remain CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery.
evidence.summary: node1 boot ID changed from 32e1f4e0-0ae4-4b67-9b90-4ddc6c4ce51e to 80841a8a-f1d0-4308-924e-5740c0b7f8f0; inetd, firewall, listener, files, and remote PONG/ERROR behavior recovered.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery.
evidence.summary: node2 boot ID changed from fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34 to 25853876-a8af-4578-b407-d1701d38436e; its files and client tooling recovered, remote protocol tests passed, and eight post-restart concurrent clients completed with zero failures.
